Functional specifications and exclusive files: add only test/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge/delivery_result_test.exs; production target lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge/delivery_result.ex remains unchanged. Do not edit test/zaq/channels/telegram_history_delivery_test.exs or test/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge_test.exs. DeliveryResult moduledoc owns edit acknowledgments; line 34 rejects any result not :ok, {:ok, _}, or {:error, _} with {:error, {:unexpected_response, original}}. Existing TelegramHistoryDeliveryTest lines 256-275 covers provider error preservation but not malformed adapter success; JidoChatBridgeTest lines 2155-2181 covers unrelated outbound typing/reaction normalization, not edit. JidoChatBridge.edit_message/7 calls DeliveryResult on the update path at line 2008. No production operation changes: Action reuse assessment not applicable (tests only, no new Action, domain API, tool, or consumer; reuse normalize_edit/2 directly). No new feature/E2E journey or UI approval gate: pure Channels edit-result contract.

Tests to add before implementation: (1) concrete regression test, use ExUnit.Case async: true and alias DeliveryResult. For adapter Jido.Chat.Mattermost.Adapter, pass unexpected atom :unexpected; assert exactly {:error, {:unexpected_response, :unexpected}}, never :ok or {:ok, _}. This alone reaches missed line 34 and proves fail-closed outcome. (2) focused bounded property with ExUnitProperties and StreamData, invariant: every generated non-success/non-error-tag edit response retains the exact original term inside unexpected_response. Construct StreamData.one_of with nil, booleans, integers, short binaries, short lists/maps, and tuples tagged :unexpected (e.g. {:unexpected, bounded integer}); exclude :ok and all {:ok, _}/{:error, _} by construction; use Mattermost adapter, check all with bounded max_runs ~50-100, exact equality of returned error and original term. Add a concrete {:unexpected, %{status: 202}} example if needed to demonstrate opaque payload preservation. Do not feed Telegram-shaped ExGram errors into this property: those are handled by earlier provider-specific clause. Existing adjacent cases already cover valid errors; no redundant Cartesian product.

Branches/paths validated: line 34 fallback for malformed atom, nil and bounded other shapes; success and tagged error branches are deliberately out of scope, already exercised nearby. Direct public normalizer tests are the smallest meaningful level; optional later bridge-level test only if coverage instrumentation proves line 34 unreachable through direct calls, not part of this exclusive scope. No mock, stub, DB, HTTP, runtime config, process, global Mox mode or Application env changes; no fixtures or shared helpers beyond ExUnitProperties/StreamData and alias; async: true; no sleeps or polling. Assertions inspect exact values rather than call order. Property is warranted by malformed-value rejection invariant; bounded generators prevent irrelevant huge terms.

Validation for implementer only (not executed during planning): mix test test/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge/delivery_result_test.exs; inspect a fresh focused coveralls.json report for target line 34 and confirm the real production module is instrumented; run mix q through Context Mode plus isolated test and final mix precommit only at workflow final human approval gate. Do not claim measured coverage from planning. Coverage target >=95% where applicable; report actual line outcome and exceptions. If no focused report or coverage tooling cannot isolate file, record exact blocker, do not alter production semantics or add test-only seam. Documentation update: none (test-only behavior-preserving addition); Beadwork plan/results remain source of truth. No secrets, permissions, cross-service calls, new Actions, or browser E2E. Unreachable blockers: none identified; if adapter type is unavailable during isolated run, replace adapter with a stable non-Telegram module atom because fallback adapter argument is ignored, document change before implementing.
